home.hero_tagline: STEAM EDUCATION AND INNOVATION FOR TERRITORIAL PEACE
home.hero_desc: We are facilitators of change, transforming realities through consulting, engineering, and education projects.
home.hero_bold: We work for the digital inclusion of vulnerable communities.
home.mission_subtitle: SAMVAL Foundation connects senior engineering with sustainable community development.
home.mission_card_desc: Democratize access to STEAM education through contextualized programs that strengthen local capacities and generate sustainable development opportunities in vulnerable territories.
home.vision_card_desc: Our goal for 2030 is to expand the reach of transformative education that connects innovation, territory, and peace, with the aspiration of positively impacting more than 100,000 people.
home.values_card_desc: Each software developed funds robotics and programming programs in the Sierra Nevada.
home.impact_desc: We don't just write code, we build futures. These are our accumulated social impact figures.
home.services_desc: We deliver high-quality technology services for companies that expect technical excellence and measurable social impact.
home.cta_bottom_title: Every line of code supports a dream in the Sierra Nevada
home.cta_bottom_desc: Ready to be part of the digital transformation with social impact?
home.hero_positioning: A pioneering culturally grounded robotics platform in Latin America: we connect educational robots with native languages and Indigenous worldviews.
home.unique_title: We are not just another robotics program
home.unique_subtitle: SAMVAL creates educational technology co-designed with communities, not imposed from the outside.
home.unique_1_desc: We create experiences where Arhuaco and Palenquero children program educational robots in Iku and Palenquero. Technology speaks their language.
home.unique_2_desc: Each learning module is designed with the community. The robot challenges integrate their worldview, stories, and territory instead of generic curricula.
home.unique_3_desc: We are building a new educational category that brings together physical robotics, cultural identity, and computational thinking for ethnic communities.
home.complement_title: Where large-scale programs do not reach
home.complement_desc: National programs may install labs and deliver equipment. None adapt the content to the language, worldview, and identity of ethnic communities the way SAMVAL does.
home.complement_1_desc: Our methodology integrates Indigenous worldviews into STEM challenges. We do not merely translate: we co-create with the community.
home.complement_2_desc: Years of fieldwork have given us something no centralized program can buy: the trust of traditional authorities.
home.complement_3_desc: We do not run four-day camps. We provide sustained support and train local leaders who can multiply the impact.

privacy_page.title: Personal Data Processing Policy
privacy_page.intro: This policy explains how SAMVAL Foundation collects, uses, stores, and protects personal data received through its forms, donations, volunteering, partnerships, and contact channels.
privacy_page.responsible_content: <0>SAMVAL Foundation</0>, identified with NIT 901.036.033-0, located at Calle 104 #51B-154 Ofi 17, Castellana Campestre, Barranquilla, Colombia, and reachable at <1>info@samval.org</1>, acts as the controller of personal data.
privacy_page.legal_basis_intro: SAMVAL processes personal data only when there is a valid basis to do so:
legal_basis_list: Prior, express, and informed authorization from the data subject when required.
Compliance with legal, accounting, tax, administrative, or regulatory obligations.
Management of pre-contractual, contractual, donation, volunteering, partnership, or service relationships.
Institutional legitimate interest to respond to requests, protect site security, and improve service channels while respecting data subject rights.
privacy_page.data_collected_intro: Depending on the form or channel used, SAMVAL Foundation may receive the following categories of data:
data_collected_list: Identification and contact data: first name, last name, email address, phone number, country, city, company, or organization.
Data related to requests, messages, volunteering interests, partnerships, technology services, or participation in programs.
Data needed to manage donations, certificates, receipts, accounting processes, or reports required by law.
Basic technical browsing data, such as IP address, device, browser, pages visited, and interaction events when measurement tools are used.
Images, testimonials, or audiovisual records of activities, only when there is authorization or another valid basis for institutional use.
privacy_page.purposes_intro: Personal data may be processed for the following institutional purposes:
purposes_list: Responding to requests submitted through contact, services, volunteering, or partnership forms.
Managing donations, issuing certificates when applicable, and meeting accounting, tax, and administrative obligations.
Communicating updates, reports, calls, and results related to social and educational programs.
Coordinating activities with partners, volunteers, beneficiaries, suppliers, and public or private entities.
Preparing statistical or impact analyses using aggregated or anonymized information whenever possible.
privacy_page.minors_content: When SAMVAL participates in activities involving children or adolescents, their data will be processed with enhanced protection, respecting their best interests and, when applicable, with authorization from parents, guardians, legal representatives, or partner institutions authorized to grant it.
privacy_page.third_parties_content: SAMVAL may rely on technology providers, form platforms, CRM systems, web hosting, email, analytics, payment gateways, communication tools, and administrative services. These third parties may process information only to operate the required services. Some providers may store or process data outside Colombia, so SAMVAL will seek to use services with reasonable security and data protection measures.
privacy_page.cookies_content: The site may use cookies or similar technologies necessary for operation, traffic measurement, browsing analysis, content improvement, and conversion tracking. These tools may generate technical or statistical data that helps evaluate site performance and the effectiveness of institutional campaigns.
privacy_page.images_content: Photographs, videos, testimonials, or stories of beneficiaries, volunteers, partners, or participants will be used for institutional, informational, or accountability purposes when there is authorization or another valid basis for publication. In activities involving minors, SAMVAL will apply enhanced protection criteria.
privacy_page.rights_intro: Under applicable Colombian regulations, data subjects may exercise the following rights:
rights_list: Access, update, correct, or request deletion of their personal data.
Request proof of the authorization granted for data processing.
Be informed about how their personal data has been used.
Withdraw authorization or request deletion when there is no legal, accounting, contractual, or tax duty requiring the information to be retained.
File complaints before the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce when appropriate.
privacy_page.procedure_content: Requests, complaints, or inquiries related to personal data may be sent to <1>info@samval.org</1>. SAMVAL will respond within the timeframes established by Law 1581 of 2012 and its regulatory provisions.
privacy_page.security_content: SAMVAL Foundation applies reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational measures to protect information against unauthorized access, loss, alteration, or misuse. Data will be retained while the purpose that justified its collection remains in place, while necessary to comply with legal, accounting, or tax obligations, or during the periods required by applicable regulations. When data is no longer needed, it will be deleted, anonymized, or securely archived as appropriate.

impact_page.title: Our Impact
impact_page.subtitle: Real data, real communities, and stories that transform lives.
impact_page.metric_1_desc: students from ethnic communities have participated in our STEAM programs
impact_page.metric_2_desc: Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities served directly
impact_page.metric_3_desc: hours of robotics and programming education delivered
impact_page.metric_4_desc: rural teachers trained in culturally grounded STEAM methodology
impact_page.map_desc: We work with communities, schools, and local partners in territories where technology can expand opportunities without displacing cultural identity.
impact_page.map_location_1_desc: Arhuaco communities — programming in Iku, educational robotics connected to the Law of Origin.
impact_page.map_location_2_desc: The first Afro-Colombian community with robotics modules in the Palenquero language. Robots that speak Palenquero.
impact_page.map_location_3_desc: Administrative headquarters and development lab. Partnerships with local universities.
impact_page.case_1_title: From the Sierra to Code: Digital Iku
impact_page.case_1_desc: In the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Arhuaco children learned to program educational robots using concepts from their Law of Origin. Community elders helped design the challenges, integrating their worldview into every module. The result: children who see technology as an extension of their culture, not a threat.
impact_page.case_1_quote: The robot understands our way of thinking about the territory.
impact_page.case_2_title: Palenque Programs: Robots in the Palenquero Language
impact_page.case_2_desc: In San Basilio de Palenque, the first free Black town in the Americas, children program in Palenquero, a Creole language not represented in government STEM programs. SAMVAL co-created the modules with local leaders, integrating music, dance, and oral tradition into the robotics challenges.
impact_page.case_2_quote: Here, the robot also dances champeta.

timeline.event: Founding members met in Switzerland to define how technology with social impact could become a reality through SAMVAL.

Field visit to the Sierra Nevada. Launch of programming languages in Indigenous languages.
Qualification under Colombia's Special Tax Regime (ESAL), strengthening transparency, measurable impact, and tax benefits for donors and strategic allies.

resources_page.module_palenquero_desc: Robotics in the Palenquero Creole language. Challenges that integrate Afro-Colombian music, dance, and oral tradition.
